venues.name: CC Atlanta
venues.narrative: **CCATL — Thursday 9/3.** Missed target: net $1,222 vs $2,150 target (−43%); food $157; 41 guests, $29.83 check avg; comps $60.90. MOD Mkz / JK. Very chill Thursday — not unusual with the holiday coming up; DragonCon is in town so anything can happen this weekend. Reminder to keep an eye on garnishes and how they're stored. Some regular faces stayed a while. Barback and Valerie knocked out prep and got a good close training. Kitchen: quiet day — use downtime to ABK. 86 plastic cups. No incidents; no-shows not charged. Favorite moment: a late group came in to celebrate a friend's first DJ set. Entered by Mya.

venues.name: CC Nashville
venues.weather: Extremely hot — heat advisory; foot traffic after sunset
venues.narrative: **CCNSH — Thursday 9/3.** Missed target: net $2,272 vs $3,487 target (−35%); food $153; ~62 guests, $36.64 check avg; comps $40.15 / 1.8% (DNL, Bingo, F&F). MOD KK/KE, Chef JMS. Under a heat advisory — slow start with only ~$300 in sales, then business picked up ~9:30pm and stayed consistent until 11:30pm, doing the bulk of sales in a short window. Lots of dates and friend groups, plus a local business that ran a $400 tab; many folks likely stayed home in the heat. Kitchen: food sales lower than hoped but everyone complimentary; JMS held down BOH and was present on the floor. Maintenance: CO2 behind the bar. No incidents; no-shows not charged. Favorite moment: industry friend Jasmine (Posty's on Broadway) visited; Sara hosted old regulars from Fleet Street Pub; Clay's friend stopped in for belated birthday wishes. Entered by JO.

venues.name: D&C Denver
venues.narrative: **DVR — Thursday 9/3.** Beat target including events: total net incl. events $18,299.14 vs $11,186 target (+64%); net ex-events $8,577.14 (DC/AM $1,135.09; D&C PM $7,320.51; Garden/6A n/a); net event sales $9,722 (event food $5,400); total food incl. events $7,432.80 (in-house $2,032.80); 251 guests (Tock); comps $314.95 (~3.67%). AM MOD/Chef: Chef Josh & Maggie; PM: Chefs Rachel & Lucas + Evan. D&C: pretty chill night — busy pop 5–7pm, then chill; never quite went on a wait; got Kayla and Kyle out decently early; event guests hung out at the bar afterwards. Kitchen (Ayu): great steady night, Lucas & Rachel killed the event. Events (Kelly): rehearsal dinner for Rachael & Marshall, 50 guests, 6–9pm in Vauxhall & the Garden — massive family-style dinner by Lucas W & Rachael; MOB thanked us profusely; event team crushed it. DC/AM: no report made. Break make-up complete; no-shows not charged; no incidents. Maintenance: same as yesterday (marquee under-bar lights won't dim; garden doors sticking on Mezz floor; VH men's stall door sticking). Favorite moments: Micah in for a drink before departing to NYC Sunday; event busy but under control; got some admin done. Entered by Evan.

venues.name: D&C East Village
venues.narrative: **EV — Thursday 9/3.** Beat target: net $6,126 vs $5,473 target (+12%); food $517, beverage $5,608; 169 covers (Sevenrooms), $36 check avg; comps $132.27 (2.2%). MOD Kyler, Chef Steves. Service: slower but even-paced evening with a slow start and end; many out-of-towners visiting friends/family for Labor Day reunions; Mari (past EV server) back to celebrate her husband's birthday with his parents; a 3-top in love with the Telegraph. Top sellers: Native Lion, Rosalie, High Plains and Paper Wasp tied. Door (HP): hot, very humid; US Open travelers and returning college students built a decent flow — filled slowly from open, a 6-top boosted energy, packed by 8:30pm; short waitlist in and out until 11pm mainly for medium groups; 2/3 full until 12:30am, silent from 1am. Guests included DCLA regulars celebrating their 15th anniversary at the OG, Ashira Green celebrating her husband's birthday, Koba, Drew from El Camino, and Alexis (Derrumbes rep). No-show: Patric Nordmark for 2 at 6:30pm (not charged). Menu count 18; breakage 1 mini coupe. Maintenance: roof leaking in basement in front of office door. Entered by Stef.

venues.name: D&C Los Angeles
venues.narrative: **LA — Thursday 9/3.** Beat target: net $6,593 vs $6,069 target (+9%); food $1,069; Marquee $6,593 (Standing Room $0); 161 guests, $88.28 check avg (as reported); comps $128.52 (member, investor, a few birthday gifts, couple of DNLs). MOD Gigi, Chef Saleh. Quite the busy night — steady start built to a full room by 7:00; when Julian arrived at 7:30 the room was completely full; waitlist from ~7:45 for most of the night. New security guard training with Landis. Analise did a great job at the host stand texting the waitlist and seating quickly; few large parties so two-tops were sat at larger tables. Waitlist died down ~11:00; Mitchell out then, Bailey off the floor around midnight; super smooth close cleared the building ~1:15. Member Matthew and partner had a wonderful time and complimented Bailey and Julian. Kitchen: everything looked awesome; a few low items but Oscar and Saleh kept things running; 86 cheese plate. Maintenance: frayed USB charging-port cable — will buy a new one for the weekend. No incidents; no-shows charged. Favorite moment: a guest called the Hollow Technique one of the best cocktails of his life, comparing it to a donut and coffee. Entered by Gigi.

venues.name: D&C Washington DC
venues.weather: Hot and humid, then heavy rain and thunderstorms
venues.narrative: **DC — Thursday 9/3.** Beat target: total net incl. events $4,386.95 vs $4,221 target (+4%); Marquee bar sales $4,835.21, Garden $0, total sales $4,835.21; food $212; 101 guests (74 walk-in / 27 reso), $38.48 check avg; comps $78.50 (industry $2.90, manager meal $24, F&F $6.60, DNL $45). MOD Josh Marcus. Slower start likely due to heat and humidity; picked up ~6:30 and the room was bopping by 8:00; tapered ~9:00; cuts at 10:00 (Devan off host stand, Tyler on side work). Light trickle until ~11:00 when lightning and thunder began; huge downpour by 11:30 kept guests in the room — planned to postpone last call, and as rain eased ~12:20 most guests had just ordered another round. Energetic group from table 44 split between bar and table when the storm hit. Special visit from Sophia and a couple of guests from Hydrox. Kitchen: very light night, many guests coming from dinner; kitchen close not checked. Went well: good energy, short ticket times, guest connections. Maintenance: ice machine slow leak; curtains. No incidents; no-shows charged. Favorite moment: people's reaction to the thunderstorm. Entered by Marcus.

venues.name: Municipal Grand F&B
venues.weather: Hot with one small mid-day rain
venues.narrative: **MG — Thursday 9/3.** Beat target: net $4,834 vs $4,000 target (+21%); Municipal Bar AM $823 / PM $2,792; Sun Club $199; Hot Eye $622; food $2,100; 79 guests (OpenTable: 4 AM + 75 PM); comps $520. AM MOD/Chef Braden & Lex; PM James & Shannon. Morning: slow, a few hotel guests for breakfast; Sierra trained Gracie on her first day. Evening: slow with lots of help — Earl had a great training shift with Carla, Jack trained Estella at the door, Madison supported the floor, Eryn and Jason had an easy night at the bar. Sun Club (Skylar): windy and warm; lights still out since yesterday; sold 3 drinks in the first hour then slowed; heavy rain ~3pm for a few minutes; banana daiquiri in the works — check with a manager before starting the frozen; deep-cleaned the frozen machine; restock espresso beans, sparkling water, tequila, passion fruit. Hot Eye: burrito & cocktail photo shoot with Kelly before open, then painfully slow. Kitchen: none. Favorite moment: photo shoot with Kelly. Entered by Alexis.

venues.name: D&C Seattle
venues.weather: High of 67, scattered showers all day and night
venues.narrative: **SEA — Thursday 9/3. First public night (opening night).** Net $11,700 (just shy of $12K); food $1,600; 230 covers, $50.86 check avg; comps $1,620 (13.8% — lots of industry friends, high DNLs as people explored the menu, and some walk-outs). Form listed a sales target of $420, which is not a real daily target (targets expected to begin week of 9/7) — recorded as no target. MOD Curtis Hayes. "Off to the races. Rollerskating on a rainbow off a comet." High energy all night; team happy and engaged; ran first actual break rotations, which went great. Issue: Toast prices differing from listed menu prices — flagged to WR and MB as a heavier back-end lift. Kitchen cranking; will have a clearer picture of prep/kitchen hours; may need to trim the menu for execution (to discuss with JS and WH). Some "borderline" guests and people trying to jump the waitlist; Fri/Sat/Sun resos may be funky from consolation-prize QR codes. Lights looked great; 9–9:30 curtain draw was the move. Bar cranked drinks with great hospitality, floor moved with urgency, hosts took charge of stacking tables. Kitchen adjusting par levels for busier services; expect plenty of 86s tomorrow. No incidents; no-shows not charged. Favorite moment: Julian's dad Joe walked around the bar, put his hands in his pockets and said "this is the best bar in the world." Entered by Curtis Hayes.
